title: Love the work (Avot 1:10)
hookLine: Shemaiah: love labor, hate lording over others, don't court the powerful
carry: half a wage, just to listen
last: A QUESTION CAN TEACH A LIE.

cards: A winter Friday in Jerusalem, a long time ago. A poor young laborer pays half his day's wage to get into the house of study. Today he has nothing left, so the guard won't let him in.
He climbs onto the roof and lies down by the skylight, just to hear the teachers talk. Snow begins to fall. He stays.
In the morning, the two teachers inside notice the room is strangely dark. They look up and find a man buried in snow across the window.
The Talmud says they carried him down, warmed him by the fire, and said he was worth it. The young man was Hillel. One of his teachers was Shemaiah.

teach.b: Shemaiah and his partner Avtalyon are the next pair in the chain of Pirkei Avot. The Talmud remembers that they came from families of converts, and they led the sages of their day. Shemaiah's saying has three short parts.
First: love work. The Hebrew word is melakhah, the same word used for the creative work that stops on Shabbat. Not just tolerate it.
Love it. Some of the sages had trades: Avot names a Rabbi Yochanan the sandal-maker, and elsewhere praises Torah study joined with work. For them, work wasn't a distraction from a holy life.
It was part of one. Second: hate rabbanut.
It sounds like being a rabbi, but here it means lording it over people, holding a title so others have to bow. Shemaiah had authority, and he warns against loving it.
Third: don't get too close to the ruling power. Later in Avot, another sage warns that rulers draw people close when it suits them and drop them when it doesn't.

Together: honest work, done gladly, without climbing over people, and without selling yourself to whoever's in charge. Now go back to the roof. Hillel spent half of every wage just to be let in to learn.
He loved the work, both kinds: the labor that paid the fee, and the learning it paid for. And the teachers who found him didn't hand him a title. They warmed him up.

how: Avot 1:10 is read as a teaching about the dignity of work, and some sages of the Mishnah and Talmud are remembered as people with trades as well as teachers.

s: Shemaiah taught that study matters more than work
his first words are love work, and Avot names sages with trades.
Hillel paid to get into the house of study
the Talmud says half his day's wage went to the guard at the door.
hate rabbanut means don't become a rabbi
here it means lording it over people, loving a title for its power.

games.q: you're Hillel. you have no money today, and the guard won't let you in to hear the teachers. what do you do?
o: go home and try next week.
climb onto the roof and listen at the skylight.
argue with the guard until he gives in.
games.why: he lay by the skylight in the falling snow, and his teachers found him in the morning and warmed him by the fire.

practice: Picture a task waiting for you: a report, a sink of dishes, a shift, homework.

Don't take in the whole mountain; find one small piece that's honestly good, like the feel of a clean counter, a problem that clicks, a customer you helped. Hold that piece in mind, and let yourself be glad of it.

wordCard.voice: Melakhah. Work, the same word used for the labor that stops on Shabbat: Shemaiah's call to love it, done gladly, with no lording over others.

carryVoice: Your line: half a wage, just to listen. The snow didn't send him home. See you tomorrow.
